message: Thanks. To start, which state do you live in? Also, how many children under 18 live with you, if any?

Got it. A few more questions: roughly how much does your household earn from work in a year, before tax? Does anyone get health insurance through a job? And roughly how much is in bank accounts and investments?
reply: Decent money, both of us work. Yes. About 130 thousand.

summary: Household: Wisconsin, two adults in their thirties, no children, not married, both working, about $130,000 combined annual earnings, at least one person has employer health insurance. At this income none of the ten programmes is likely to apply: SNAP, WIC, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, CHIP, EITC, the refundable child tax credit, ACA premium tax credit and free school meals all have income or household-type limits this household exceeds (and there are no children, so CTC, CHIP and school meals don't apply). No applications recommended. Caveat: this is based on the answers given; if income or household changes substantially, rescreen.
